exact_statement: For independent receptor-event counts Y_i~Pois(mu_i) under H0 and Y_i~Pois(q mu_i) under H1, q=exp(delta/lambda), every decoder with worst-case binary error <= epsilon<1/2 requires M=sum_i mu_i >= -log(4 epsilon (1-epsilon))/(sqrt(q)-1)^2. As delta/lambda->0 at fixed epsilon, M >= [4 log(1/(4 epsilon (1-epsilon)))+o(1)] (lambda/delta)^2.
assumptions: Known exponential decay length lambda and known cell positions.
The two boundary-pattern hypotheses differ by a global exponential-profile displacement delta; equivalently, the entire concentration profile is multiplied by exp(delta/lambda).
Unsaturated independent Poisson event counts are the full morphogen information available to cells during the observation window.
Any cell-cell relay, gene circuit, and output decoder is stochastic postprocessing of the count vector.
No unknown additive background, receptor heterogeneity, extra spatial cue, or count correlations are included.
status: proved_model_statement_in_REPORT.md; established-prior-art-overlap-likely; no biological validation or novelty claim
novelty_boundary: The closest prior art already derives positional precision limits for noisy exponential morphogen gradients, explicitly models noisy multicellular communication, studies cell-cell refinement of morphogen boundaries, and studies amplitude-induced boundary shifts and production-cost/precision tradeoffs. The present note contributes only the exact finite-error Poisson testing form with total expected raw receptor events charged across all cells and arbitrary downstream stochastic postprocessing. Priority is unverified; treat it as a useful theorem/baseline, not a new biological principle.

costs.charged: M, total expected morphogen-receptor event count under H0 across all cells and all included temporal samples in the observation window.
not_charged: cell-cell signaling molecules, relay noise, and communication delay
downstream gene-expression resources and implementation time

falsifier_or_scope_check: Measure cell-resolved receptor-event counts under calibrated exponential profiles separated by delta, checking Poisson dispersion, cross-cell correlations, global scaling, and event totals. Non-Poisson or correlated observations do not refute the theorem but invalidate its biological likelihood model and require a replacement calculation.
next_gate: Match this bound against Tostevin, ten Wolde, and Howard (2007), especially their single-gradient threshold-position variance and temporal averaging, using the same observation time, receptor-event budget, tissue geometry, and noise model. Retain as baseline or redirect unless the matched comparison yields a new consequence.
